title: PRD: Lightweight compatibility signals and versioning contract for community model intake
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Define a lightweight, machine-readable set of compatibility signals and a versioning contract that community/open models must provide during catalog intake. Goal is to reduce manual runtime mismatches, prevent silent regressions after model updates, and provide clear rules for when Redwood should automatically pin, mark for human review, or allow unpinned variants for serving. This PRD focuses on intake metadata, acceptance gates, runtime fallback semantics, and monitoring requirements; it does not mandate model quality thresholds or full benchmark pipelines (those are separate).
compatibility_signals: We will require a short compatibility metadata block in the model catalog entry with the following signals: 1) architecture_hint (e.g., gpt2-like, llama-family, transformer-xl) 2) kv_cache_behavior: {"preserved"|"reset_on_new_key"|"unknown"} 3) tensor_layout_hint: {"standard"|"transposed"|"custom"} 4) supported_max_seq_length (integer tokens) 5) quantization_safe: {"none"|"int8"|"int4"|"mixed"} 6) tokenizer_family (e.g., sentencepiece, gpt2, byte-level) 7) recommended_runtime_variant (e.g., "baseline", "kv-optimized") 8) semver_like_tag (free text but recommended format vMAJOR.MINOR[+meta]). These signals are intentionally compact to be machine-checked at intake and by the runtime routing layer.
versioning_contract: Contract rules: 1) Model providers must supply a version string. We recommend semver-like tags but accept other conventions; Redwood will parse MAJOR.MINOR when possible. 2) Any change to MAJOR indicates breaking runtime changes and must be treated as incompatible -> automatic pin. 3) MINOR or PATCH updates that do not modify architecture_hint or kv_cache_behavior may be considered compatible; runtime may allow unpinned rollout if manifest includes a compatibility_digest (SHA256 of key model artifacts). 4) If provider cannot or will not include compatibility_digest, the model is defaulted to 'review_required' for unpinned updates. 5) Providers may include an explicit 'compatibility_declared: true' boolean to fast-track intake. 6) Redwood reserves the right to override declared compatibility based on runtime profiling results.
onboarding_checklist: Intake checklist for PM/Eng/Registry: 1) Model metadata filled (all compatibility signals). 2) Version string present and formatted. 3) Tokenizer artifact attached and verified by ingest script. 4) Quick runtime smoke test (inference for short prompt) passes on baseline runtime. 5) Compatibility digest present or manual attest by model owner. 6) Evals: run a small acceptance prompt set (10-20 prompts) for basic decoding sanity. 7) Security scan of artifacts (dependency check). 8) Mark entry as 'pinned' / 'untested_unpinned' / 'trusted_unpinned' based on outcome. 9) Add monitoring hooks and baseline metrics (latency, OOM rate, token error rate).
runtime_fallback_policy: Fallback rules to keep serving healthy: 1) If an unpinned variant fails smoke test at runtime (OOM, kernel mismatch, decoding errors), route requests to pinned MAJOR-compatible variant. 2) If pinned variant absent, fallback to Redwood-verified baseline model with similar capability. 3) Fallback should increment a catalog-level fallback counter and emit an alert if >0.5% of requests in 5m window hit fallback. 4) For latency-sensitive customers, prefer routing to dedicated capacity variants before fallback to lower-tier models.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance criteria for this ticket: 1) Intake UI and API accept the new compact compatibility block and enforce required fields. 2) Backend validation rejects entries missing architecture_hint or tokenizer_family. 3) Automated parser extracts MAJOR.MINOR when possible and flags ambiguous version strings for review. 4) Ingest smoke test harness runs on CI and returns pass/fail for a submitted model artifact. 5) A runtime routing policy exists that reads compatibility_signals and applies fallback rules described. 6) Dashboard shows compatibility status and counts of pinned vs unpinned models. 7) Documentation and onboarding checklist published in Confluence with examples. 8) End-to-end test demonstrating an unpinned model causing a fallback and alert generation in staging.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to capture: 1) compatibility_validation_failures (counter) 2) fallback_rate_by_model (percent per 5m) 3) smoke_test_failures_during_intake (counter) 4) runtime_compat_mismatch_errors (counter with tags: model, version) 5) manual_review_queue_size. Alerts: 1) Fallback rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P1 alert to runtime-oncall. 2) Intake smoke test failure rate > 10% in a day -> Notify model-catalog team. 3) Compatibility validation failures > 20 in a day -> PM review. All metrics must be visible in the Console and have per-model drilldowns.
rollout_strategy: Phased rollout: 1) Implement intake validation and storage in staging only for 2 weeks. 2) Enable parser and dashboard read-only in production to collect signals without blocking (observability window). 3) After 2 weeks and no major issues, enable enforcement on new catalog entries. 4) Backfill existing catalog entries with a best-effort parser and mark those with missing signals as 'needs_manifest_update'. 5) Only allow automatic unpinned updates for models with declared compatibility_digest and passing smoke tests. 6) Communicate changes to community model providers via repo/announcements and provide a helper script for manifest generation.
risks_and_mitigations: 1) Risk: False positives in compatibility detection block good models -> Mitigation: Observability window and opt-out for small/experimental providers. 2) Risk: Providers cannot produce compatibility_digest -> Mitigation: manual attestation + small smoke test acceptance path. 3) Risk: Additional operational burden on registry team -> Mitigation: automation of checks and clear UI guidance. 4) Risk: Overly strict version parsing -> Mitigation: fallback to heuristic tagging and manual-review flags.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose compact signal set to minimize barrier to entry. 2026-03-05: Agreed that MAJOR-level changes are breaking by default and will enforce pinning. 2026-03-10: Decided to require tokenizer_family and architecture_hint as mandatory fields. 2026-03-12: Opted to accept non-semver tags but attempt MAJOR.MINOR parse heuristics; ambiguous tags flagged for review.

summary: Provides a pragmatic, minimally invasive compatibility and versioning contract for community/open models to reduce runtime surprises, automate sensible pinning behavior, and provide clear acceptance gates for new catalog entries while preserving low-friction onboarding for experimental providers.
